notes: Built from docs/library/padel.md by scripts/build-padel-library.js; edit padel.md, then rebuild. One version for every player (no playing side). Scores come from the existing scoring engine, unchanged. Words in curly brackets are filled in by the engine from the athlete's results; Gemini never writes or changes these lines. plain_name, measures and weapon (headline, body, evenness) are PeakPerformance wording added for the report, not text from padel.md.
draft_notice_help: Shown in the footer of every page of the padel athlete report. Set draft_notice to null (or "") to switch it off; applies to reports generated after the change. Kept when the library is rebuilt.

target.label: Gold
target.text: Tier target is the Gold line (score 75). Priorities are ranked by score points below 75, biggest gap first; ties keep library order.

plan.text: One combined 6-week plan: every selected fix runs from week 1. A fix shorter than 6 weeks switches to that test's maintain fix (where the library has one) for the remaining weeks.

fault_words.heels_knees: heels lifted or knees caved in
fault_words.arms_back: arms dropped forward or lower back arched

tests.name: 10m Sprint
tests.what_we_measured: How fast you cover 10 metres from a standing start, the length of one side of the court.
tests.notice: you see the lob coming but your opponents get back to the net before you do, or you reach balls off the side glass stretching instead of set.

why.label: Below target
why.text: You covered 10 metres in {time}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} away.

why.label: At Gold
why.text: You covered 10 metres in {time}. That's Gold level.

tests.fix_it: you'll win more races back to the net, and that's where padel points are won.

rules.text: Score below tier target → show Fix A: first-step power.
At or above Gold → show Fix B: keep it sharp.

A.title: first-step power
exercises: Falling starts over 5 metres: 6 reps, full rest.
Split-step then sprint on a partner's call: 6 reps.
Split squats: 3 sets of 8 each leg.

B.title: keep it sharp
exercises: Split-step reaction sprints over 5 metres: 6 reps.

court_drills: Back-to-net sprints: from the back glass to the net, then split-step. 6 reps.
Turn and chase: a partner lobs over you; turn and run it down before it reaches the back glass. 8 reps.

weapon.headline: Quick off the mark
weapon.body: you are quick over the first few steps

tests.name: 5-0-5 Agility Test
tests.what_we_measured: How quickly you sprint, stop, turn 180° and sprint back out.
tests.notice: the ball comes off the back glass at an odd angle and you're already moving the wrong way, or you get pulled wide and can't get back in time to cover the middle.

why.label: Below target
why.text: You turned and came back in {time}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} away.

why.label: One side slower
why.text: You turn {gap}% slower off your {weaker_side} foot.

tests.fix_it: you'll stop, turn and reach more balls on balance, point after point.

rules.text: Time slower than tier target → show Fix A: brake and turn.
Slower turning off one foot than the other (if timed both ways, more than 5%, proposed) → also show Fix B: even both turns.

A.title: brake and turn
exercises: Deceleration drills: sprint 5 metres, stop in two steps and hold. 6 reps.
5-0-5 practice at 80% effort, focusing on a low turn: 6 reps.
Lateral lunges: 3 sets of 8 each side.

B.title: even both turns
exercises: Two extra turns off your weaker foot in each session.

court_drills: Back-glass exits: a partner feeds into the corner; turn and play it out. 10 reps.
Cover-the-middle shuffle: shuffle wide, plant and return to centre. 3 sets of 6.

tests.name: Ruler Drop Test
tests.what_we_measured: How far a dropped ruler falls before you catch it. Shorter is faster.
tests.nickname: Reaction: how fast you see and move
tests.notice: fast exchanges at the net go past you before your racket is ready, or a smash off the glass catches you late.

why.label: Below target
why.text: You caught the ruler at {distance}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} away.

why.label: At Gold
why.text: You caught the ruler at {distance}. That's Gold level.

tests.fix_it: you'll win more of the quick-fire volleys at the net, and have time to set your racket against smashes.

rules.text: Catch distance worse than tier target → show Fix A: sharpen reactions.
At or above Gold → show Fix B: keep it sharp.

A.title: sharpen reactions
exercises: Reaction ball against a wall: 3 rounds of 60 seconds.
Partner drops: a partner drops a ball without warning; catch it before the second bounce. 3 sets of 10.

B.title: keep it sharp
exercises: Fast volley rallies at the net once a week.

court_drills: Quick-fire volleys with a partner, both at the net: 3 rounds of 30 seconds.
A partner feeds fast balls at your body; volley each one. 20 balls.
tests.retest_note: Reaction improves fastest, so it's often the first stat that moves.

tests.name: Overhead Squat
tests.what_we_measured: How well your ankles, hips, upper back and shoulders work together as you squat with your arms overhead.
tests.nickname: Movement: getting low and reaching high
tests.notice: your back gets tired in long defensive rallies, or bandejas and smashes feel cramped, like you can't get your arm fully up.

why.label: Heels lifting or knees caving
why.text: As you squatted, your {fault}. Tight ankles or weak hips stop you getting low while keeping good posture.

why.label: Arms dropping or back arching
why.text: As you squatted, your {fault}. A stiff upper back or tight shoulders make your lower back do the work on overheads.

why.label: No fault recorded
why.text: Your coach will go through what they saw and pick the right fix with you.

tests.fix_it: you can stay low all rally and hit overheads standing tall, without your lower back paying for it.

rules.text: Heels lifting or knees caving → show Fix A: ankles and hips.
Arms dropping forward or the lower back arching → show Fix B: shoulders and upper back.
Clean pattern → show Fix C: maintain.

A.title: ankles and hips
exercises: Knee-to-wall ankle stretch: 2 sets of 10 each side.
Goblet squat holds at the bottom: 3 holds of 30 seconds.
Banded lateral walks: 2 sets of 12 steps each way.

B.title: shoulders and upper back
exercises: Foam roller extensions on the upper back: 10 slow reps.
Wall slides: 2 sets of 10.
Open book stretch: 2 sets of 10 each side.

C.title: maintain
exercises: Overhead squats with a stick in every warm-up: 1 set of 8.

court_drills: Low-ball feeds: a partner feeds at your feet; stay low and play them back. 15 balls.
Shadow bandejas, keeping your chest tall: 2 sets of 10.

weapon.headline: Low and tall when it counts
weapon.body: your ankles, hips, upper back and shoulders work well together when you squat with your arms overhead

tests.name: Trunk Rotation
tests.what_we_measured: How far your upper body turns to each side while your hips stay still.
tests.notice: your víbora and smash lack spin and pace even when you swing hard, or your forehand feels like it's all arm.

why.label: One side tighter
why.text: Your upper body turns {gap}% less to the {weaker_side} than to the other side.

why.label: Both sides below target
why.text: Your rotation scored {score}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} points away.

tests.fix_it: you'll get more spin and pace on overheads and drives, without forcing your shoulder.

rules.text: One side more than 10% less than the other (proposed) → show Fix A: even it out.
Both sides below tier target → show Fix B: open up the upper back.

A.title: even it out
exercises: Open book stretch toward the tighter side: 2 sets of 10, plus one extra set on that side.
Seated rotations with a stick across your shoulders: 2 sets of 10 each side.

B.title: open up the upper back
exercises: Foam roller extensions on the upper back: 10 slow reps.
Open book: 2 sets of 10 each side.
Half-kneeling band rotations: 3 sets of 10 each side.

court_drills: Med ball side throws against a wall: 3 sets of 6 each side.
Back-glass feeds: let the ball come off the glass, turn and play it out. 10 each side.

evenness.even: almost the same to each side

tests.name: Single Leg Stand, Eyes Closed
tests.what_we_measured: How steady you stay on one leg with your eyes closed, on each side. This tests the balance system in your ankle and body, not your eyesight.
tests.notice: you wobble after a wide lunge or after landing from a smash, or you've rolled an ankle before.

why.label: Below target
why.text: With your eyes closed, you held steady for {seconds} seconds. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} away.

why.label: One leg weaker
why.text: Your {weaker_side} leg held steady for {gap}% less time than your other leg.

tests.fix_it: you'll play controlled shots off wide lunges, recover faster, and protect your ankles against sprains.

rules.text: Time held below tier target on either leg → show Fix A: build balance.
One leg holding more than 20% less time than the other (proposed) → also show Fix B: even it out. Ask about past ankle sprains on that side.
rules.coach_note: Ask about past ankle sprains on that side.

A.title: build balance
exercises: Single-leg stands, eyes open then closed: 3 holds of 30 seconds each leg.
Single-leg stands on a cushion or folded towel: 3 holds of 30 seconds each leg.
Single-leg reaches in three directions: 2 sets of 6 each leg.

B.title: even it out
exercises: One extra hold on your weaker leg in every exercise.

court_drills: Wide lunge, then hold on one leg for 2 seconds before recovering: 3 sets of 6 each side.
Small jump, land on one leg and hold for 3 seconds: 3 sets of 5 each leg.

weapon.headline: Steady on one leg
weapon.body: you stay steady on one leg with your eyes closed, {evenness}

evenness.even: almost the same on each leg

tests.name: Shoulder External Rotation Strength
tests.what_we_measured: The strength of the muscles at the back of each shoulder that rotate your arm outward.
tests.nickname: Shoulder strength: the brakes on your arm
tests.notice: your smashes and víboras lose pace late in a match, or your shoulder or elbow aches the day after.

why.label: Below target
why.text: Your racket arm scored {score}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} points away.

why.label: Racket arm weaker
why.text: Your racket arm is {gap}% weaker than your other arm. Every overhead is a fast swing and a hard stop, and the back of the shoulder does the stopping.

tests.fix_it: you can keep hitting hard overheads all match, and get through a full season without shoulder or elbow pain.

rules.text: Strength relative to bodyweight below tier target on your racket arm → show Fix A: strengthen the back of the shoulder.
Racket arm more than 10% weaker than the other arm (proposed) → also show Fix B: close the gap.
Strong and balanced → show Fix C: maintain.

A.title: strengthen the back of the shoulder
exercises: Side-lying external rotation with a light dumbbell: 3 sets of 12–15.
Band external rotation with the arm at shoulder height (90/90): 3 sets of 12.
Prone Y and T raises: 2 sets of 10 in the warm-up.

B.title: close the gap
exercises: One extra set on your racket arm for each exercise.

C.title: maintain
exercises: Band external rotation, 2 sets of 15, twice a week.

court_drills: Band external rotation before every match: 1 set of 15.
Limit full-power smashes in practice to 20–30 per session while you build strength.
Stop and tell us if you feel pain on the outside of your elbow; don't play through it.

weapon.headline: A shoulder built for overheads
weapon.body: the back of your shoulders is strong and {evenness}

tests.name: Hip Abduction Strength
tests.what_we_measured: The strength of the muscles on the outside of each hip that push your leg out to the side.
tests.notice: you're a step late to balls through the middle, or your knee drifts inward when you lunge.

why.label: Below target
why.text: Your outer hips scored {score}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} points away.

why.label: One side weaker
why.text: Your {weaker_side} side is {gap}% weaker than your other side.

tests.fix_it: you'll get a faster first step sideways and straighter knees on every lunge.

rules.text: Strength relative to bodyweight below tier target → show Fix A: build hip strength.
One side more than 10% weaker than the other (proposed) → also show Fix B: close the gap.
Strong and even → show Fix C: maintain.

A.title: build hip strength
exercises: Side-lying leg raises: 3 sets of 15 each side, slow on the way down.
Banded lateral walks: 3 sets of 12 steps each way.
Side planks with top-leg raise: 3 sets of 8 each side.

B.title: close the gap
exercises: One extra set of each exercise on the weaker side.

C.title: maintain
exercises: Banded lateral walks in every warm-up.

court_drills: Lateral push-offs: shuffle and push off to the centre line. 3 sets of 6 each way.
Lunges toward the side glass, knee tracking over the toes: 3 sets of 8 each side.
tests.retest_note: Read this alongside Hip Adduction: the balance between the two matters as much as either number.

weapon.headline: Fast first step to the middle
weapon.body: your outer hips are strong and {evenness}

tests.name: Hip Adduction Strength
tests.what_we_measured: The strength of the inner thigh (groin) muscles that pull your leg back toward the middle, on each side.
tests.nickname: Groin strength: your pull back to the middle
tests.notice: you reach a wide ball but you're slow getting back, or you feel a pull in your inner thigh after a deep lunge.

why.label: Weak compared with outer hip
why.text: Your groin is {ratio}% as strong as your outer hip. We want it at 80% or more.

why.label: One side weaker
why.text: Your {weaker_side} side is {gap}% weaker than your other side.

tests.fix_it: you'll recover faster after wide balls, with less risk of a groin strain when you lunge into the corner.

rules.text: Adduction less than 80% of abduction on the same side (proposed) → show Fix A: strengthen the groin.
One side more than 10% weaker than the other (proposed) → also show Fix B: close the gap.
Balanced and even → show Fix C: maintain.

A.title: strengthen the groin
exercises: Copenhagen plank, short lever (knee on the bench): 3 holds of 15–20 seconds each side.
Side-lying inner leg raises: 3 sets of 12 each side.
Ball squeezes between the knees: 3 holds of 10 seconds.

B.title: close the gap
exercises: One extra set on your weaker side for each exercise.

C.title: maintain
exercises: Copenhagen plank twice a week: 2 holds of 20 seconds each side.

court_drills: Lateral lunge and push back to centre: 3 sets of 8 each side.
Leg swings side to side before every match: 10 each leg.

weapon.headline: Quick recovery to the centre
weapon.body: your groin muscles are strong and {evenness}
